skill.name: deed-page
skill.description: Publish files to a public deed.page URL only when the user asks to publish, deploy, host, or share a link. Create-only stays local. Hosting is public; publish only a clean output folder. No account.
skill.summary: Publish approved static files to public deed.page links with upload previews, filename exclusions, and reusable owner tokens.
skill.author: f-o-x11

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts identify test fixtures, exclusion rules, Markdown, or JavaScript strings; no evidence found of malicious intent or audit-directed prompt injection. One confirmed network finding forwards owner credentials to an unvalidated finalization URL. Semantic findings cover insecure shell temporary files, top-level symlink bypasses, and incomplete token masking.

remediation.issue: Owner credentials are sent to an unvalidated finalization URL.
remediation.suggestion: Require finalization URLs to match the configured HTTPS origin before attaching credentials. Reject unexpected origins, schemes, and redirects.

remediation.issue: Predictable shared temporary paths can disclose uploads and minted tokens or redirect filesystem writes.
remediation.suggestion: Create one private directory using mktemp -d under umask 077. Place archives, staging, and response files inside it and clean up only that directory.

remediation.issue: Top-level symlinks can bypass sensitive-name and symlink exclusions.
remediation.suggestion: Reject symlink inputs before following them in both publishers. Add regression tests for file aliases and directory aliases targeting excluded paths.

remediation.issue: Shell token masking and extraction depend on compact JSON formatting.
remediation.suggestion: Parse responses with a structured JSON parser, redact token fields before logging, and test compact, spaced, and multiline responses.

semantic_findings.title: Predictable Shell Temporary Files Expose Content and Tokens
semantic_findings.description: Temporary paths use a predictable process ID and counter without exclusive creation or private permissions. Local users can read uploads or token responses, or precreate symlinks that redirect writes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code uses mkdir -p and curl -o on predictable shared temporary paths. No private umask or atomic temporary-directory creation protects these files.

semantic_findings.title: Top-Level Symlinks Bypass Sensitive Filename Filtering
semantic_findings.description: Both publishers follow the selected input using file or directory checks before rejecting symlinks. A benign-looking input alias can expose a sensitive target despite documented symlink exclusion.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Top-level checks follow symlinks, and filename exclusions inspect the alias name. Only entries encountered during recursive traversal receive explicit symlink rejection.

semantic_findings.title: Shell Response Logging Can Reveal Owner Tokens
semantic_findings.description: The shell publisher redacts only compact token fields before printing the response to stderr. Valid JSON whitespace between the key and value bypasses masking and exposes credentials in logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The sed pattern requires an exact compact token field. A valid response containing whitespace after the colon is printed unchanged.

content.user_title: Publish Static Files to Public deed.page Links
content.value_statement: Sharing generated static files often requires hosting setup. This skill publishes approved files to public deed.page links and saves an owner token for later updates.
actual_capabilities: Publish a static file or folder and return its public deed.page URL.
Preview selected filenames and skipped paths with dry-run mode before uploading.
Exclude common credential filenames, hidden metadata, dependencies, and symlinks encountered during directory traversal.
Prefer recognized build folders when a selected path looks like a project root.
Use the Node helper for larger uploads, hashing files and transferring missing blobs.
Reuse saved owner tokens for updates and document deletion, expiration, and single-page application routing.
limitations: The default workflow publishes publicly accessible static files, not server applications or databases.
Filename filtering does not inspect file contents and does not reliably reject top-level symlink aliases.
Publishing requires network access and curl; folders require tar, and larger uploads require Node 18 or newer.
Service plan quotas apply, the large-upload helper rejects individual files above 100 MiB, and lost tokens can prevent site management.

use_cases.description: Publish a reviewed report as a public link after removing confidential information.

use_cases.description: Preview the build folder, review exclusions, and publish a prototype with optional single-page application routing.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [report file] for public sharing and preview its publish filename without uploading. Report any confidential content or unsafe path.

prompt_templates.title: Publish an Approved Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish [approved HTML report] publicly on deed.page with slug [slug]. Save the owner token privately and return only the link and storage location.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy a Build Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Preview [build folder] and its excluded paths. After I approve the exact file list, publish it with SPA routing and expiration [seconds].

prompt_templates.title: Update a Large Static Site
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [output folder] for updating [slug]. Show the file list and upload method, then wait for approval before reusing the private owner token.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: manage a larger existing deployment

output_examples.input: Preview a build folder containing index.html, app.js, and an environment file.
Publish the approved public report and keep its management token private.
output: Owner token saved in private local storage.
The token value is not displayed.

output_examples.input: Publish a project root that has no recognized build folder.
output: Publishing stopped because the selected path looks like a project root.
No recognized build folder was found.
Select a clean output folder or explicitly authorize the root override.

best_practices: Review the exact output files and their contents before authorizing public publication.
Protect owner tokens in private durable storage and use only a trusted HTTPS service origin.
Preview uploads with dry-run mode and reject top-level symlink inputs until the exclusion bypass is fixed.
anti_patterns: Publishing a project checkout or private report because filename exclusions appear sufficient.
Uploading after a create-only request or during an unattended run without explicit publishing authorization.
Displaying owner tokens, committing them, or placing them inside published files.

faq.question: Is a deed.page account required?
faq.answer: The documented workflow requires no account signup. The first unauthenticated publish returns an owner token that must be saved privately.

faq.question: Are published files private?
faq.answer: No. The default workflow creates public links. Do not publish secrets or confidential material.

faq.question: Does creating a page automatically publish it?
faq.answer: No. A create-only request stays local. Uploading requires a publishing request or explicit confirmation.

faq.question: Does the exclusion list guarantee that secrets stay local?
faq.answer: No. Filtering uses filenames, not content inspection. Top-level symlink aliases can also bypass exclusions, so review all selected files.

faq.question: How are larger folders uploaded?
faq.answer: The shell publisher switches to the Node 18+ helper around its configured archive threshold. The helper plans uploads and sends missing blobs.

faq.question: How can I update or remove a published site?
faq.answer: Updates reuse the saved owner token. The instructions also document authenticated deletion, which requires a user request.
